title: LLMs learn scientific taste from institutional traces across the social sciences

model.params_source: paper SM1/SM2 (deterministic first-token log-probability classification over the four tier tokens); temperature and top_logprobs assumed for the chat API emulation; max_tokens raised 1 -> 4 so the whole tier word is generated for the text parse (logprobs/top_logprobs still requested and archived)

task.subset_rule: all 120 management benchmark pitches (30 per tier)
task.approximation: restricted-vocabulary first-token scoring is emulated with the chat API's top-20 logprobs (tier tokens outside the top-20 get zero mass); the placement of the pitch after the prompt is not printed; text-argmax emulation: the reply's tier word (temperature 0, 4 tokens) is scored instead of the restricted first-token log-probability argmax; identical whenever the top token is one of the four tiers (the archived top-20 logprobs allow the exact SM1 rule later)

items.source: FutureTech-OB/ai-taste, data/management_deep_probe/benchmark/management_benchmark_120.jsonl (fields title, journal, domain, level, rq_with_context; head verified)

prompt.user_template:
You are an expert in social science research. Read the research idea below and estimate its likely publication potential based on its scholarly contribution.
- Exceptional: Field-defining work with strong theoretical or empirical contribution. It would influence how researchers across the social sciences think about an important problem.
- Strong: Clear and meaningful contribution. It advances theory, evidence, or method in a non-trivial way and would be well regarded by scholars in the field.
- Fair: Competent but incremental. It extends existing knowledge in a predictable way, with limited novelty, scope, or broader significance.
- Limited: Weak contribution. The question is narrow, obvious, poorly motivated, or methodologically insufficient to support a meaningful scholarly advance.
# IMPORTANT
- Do not use search capabilities to look up information about this idea
# OUTPUT FORMAT
Respond with EXACTLY ONE of these four notations:
- Exceptional
- Strong
- Fair
- Limited
Output only the tier notation in your final answer.

{pitch}
prompt.source_location: Supplementary Methods 2 (SM2), 'Pre-specified evaluation prompt (used for SFT training, SFT evaluation, base controls, and frontier controls)'
prompt.verbatim: full for the prompt text; the position of the pitch (appended after the prompt) is assumed

placeholders_prose.pitch: items.rq_with_context (the research idea), placed after the instruction block

output.parse: label from set [Exceptional, Strong, Fair, Limited]
output.postprocess: if none of the four tokens appears in the top-20 logprobs the item is unresolved and scored as incorrect (paper: <1% unresolved)
output.parse_prose: first-token top logprobs: probability mass of the tokens that start 'Exceptional', 'Strong', 'Fair', 'Limited' (case-insensitive, leading space ignored), softmax-normalized over the four; argmax with ties broken in the alphabetical order exceptional < fair < limited < strong (SM1)

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: four-class accuracy (%) of the argmax tier against level over the 120 pitches
metric.original_location: Table ST13c (GPT-4.1-nano SFT versus architecture-matched base), row Management, column Base accuracy (SFT 57.5)

notes: The base value sits at chance (25%), so agreement is weakly informative; the prediction records in data/management_deep_probe/predictions/ (with logp dictionaries) allow a direct per-item comparison. Confidence = exp(max logprob) as in SM7. Benchmark 'level' values are the journal tiers top / top- / good / fair; the released prediction records (predictions/sft_predictions.jsonl, field rank) map them one-to-one to exceptional / strong / fair / limited (30 each), encoded in items.label_map.
